newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK/GREECE SAYS TO CUT DISCOUNT, LOMBARD BY 100BPS.
newsitem.headline: BANK/GREECE SAYS TO CUT DISCOUNT, LOMBARD BY 100BPS.

text.p: Bank of Greece, the country's central bank, said in a statement that it will slash its discount, Lombard and overdraft rates by 100 basis points to 14.5, 19 and 24 percent respectively on Tuesday, May 13.

The central bank said it decided to cut its discount, Lombard and overdraft rates to bring them closer to its intervention rate in the interbank market and account for the reduction of inflation by 1.4 percent in the first four months of 1997.
Greek CPI inflation eased to 5.9 percent year-on-year in April from 6.0 percent in March.

Bank of Greece uses a two-tier deposit facility for intervention purposes in the interbank market with the basic rate set at 11.90 percent for amounts up to 300 billion drachmas and a floor rate of 9.90 percent for sums above it. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
